responses.mission_1.search: So both BFS and A* are  13.5m, but A* expanded 228 fewer nodes than BFS because of its guide that is used for the search of the goal, while BFS explores each cell in order of discovery.
responses.mission_1.failure: On the constrained map, BFS found the shortest path at 24.5 m; however, DFS found the longer path of 50m because BFS explores cells level by level, whereas DFS follows one path for a while before it has to backtrack. IDDFS hits the resource limit because it repeatedly searches with increasing depth limits. For the unreachable map, BFS, DFS, and A* returned no_path; however, IDDFS returned resource limit.  No path means the search finished and found no route; resource limit means the algorithm ran out of allowed expansions before finishing. I used AI to help me fully understand what each algorithm is and how they work, as well as to help me implement each of the algorithms. I always verify and ensure I understand how everything is implemented. This allowed me to understand what each search algorithm resulted in on each map and understand the reasoning behind it.
responses.mission_2.prediction: I pick both A* and BFS; however, I predict that A* will finish quicker than BFS on the constrained map because A* has a heuristic guide to help search towards the goal, while BFS explores more paths without considering the true direction of the goal.
responses.mission_2.performance: Both A* and BFS were successful on the constrained map; A* took 91.204 seconds and traveled 24.05 meters, while BFS took 90.210 seconds and traveled 23.98 meters.  My original prediction was wrong: A* would finish first; however, it was BFS that finished first. Both planners had the same planned path length of 24.5 meters.
responses.mission_2.choice: I chose PRM as my delivery planner because it succeeded on both maps and was faster than A*. On the open map, PRM finished in 35.556 seconds compared to A* at 46.152 seconds. On the constrained map, PRM finished in 74.980 seconds compared to A* at 91.204 seconds. PRM also traveled a shorter distance on both maps. I think faster navigation while successfully reaching the destination is the biggest advantage for deliveries.
responses.mission_3.prediction: I compared the field settings by increasing the repulsion strength from 0.75 to 1.50 between the two social numbers. On the first preview map, social_1 completed its path, while social_2 got stuck oscillating. This shows that stronger repulsion doesn't always improve the path because the robot can get stuck instead of moving around the person.
responses.mission_3.comparison: For A*, social_1 had the largest minimum clearance of 0.805 m, compared with the baseline of 0.713 m. It also reduced time inside personal space from 1.8 seconds to 0 seconds, while taking slightly longer to finish. For RRT, social_1 increased clearance from 1.719 m to 1.723 m, and both had 0 seconds inside personal space. RRT social_1 was slightly faster but traveled a little farther. A* social_2 failed because of oscillation, so I wouldn't use it as an improvement.
responses.mission_3.recommendation: I would choose A* with social_1 because it successfully reached the goal and maintained a minimum clearance of 0.805 m. It finished in 46.434 seconds, compared to the baseline at 46.178 seconds with only 0.713 m clearance. The small increase in time for me seems worth the improvement in personal space. However, these tests only used stationary people, so we don't show how the robot would react to people suddenly moving or crossing its path.
responses.final.synthesis: I think a good robot path needs to balance speed, distance, safety, and reliability.  In Mission 2, BFS finished slightly faster than A* on the constrained map; this shows that planning efficiency doesn't always mean faster navigation. In Mission 3, adding social awareness improved A*'s clearance from 0.713 m to 0.805 m, but stronger repulsion could cause the robot to get stuck. Planned paths are always estimates, whereas the simulation results show how the robot actually performed.
responses.final.course_reflection: This activity made me more interested in robotics because I got to see how different algorithms affect a robot's navigation in real situations. I enjoyed testing the planners and comparing their results instead of just learning about them in theory. It also motivated me to explore more robotics projects in the future, especially ones involving autonomous navigation and programming.
